examples.en: Please empty the sink strainer every day.

examples.ko: 거름망이 막혀서 물이 잘 안 내려가요.
examples.en: The strainer is clogged, so the water doesn't drain well.

examples.ko: 차를 우릴 때 거름망에 찻잎을 넣어요.
examples.en: When I steep tea, I put the tea leaves in a strainer.
I bought a new strainer at the mart.

examples.ko: 음식물 찌꺼기는 거름망에 모이니까 자주 버려요.
examples.en: Food scraps collect in the strainer, so I throw them out often.
If you strain the broth through a sieve, it is clearer.

explain: 주방 싱크대나 차, 국물을 거를 때 쓰는 도구를 말해요. 체나 '채망'이라고 부르는 사람도 있지만, 싱크대 배수구에 끼우는 것은 보통 '거름망'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the tool used at the kitchen sink or for straining tea and broth. Some people say '체' or '채망', but the one that sits in a sink drain is usually called '거름망'.

examples.en: The framework construction of the building is almost finished.
This house was built with a wooden frame.
There was a fire and only the frame was left.
A building lasts long only if its frame is sturdy.

examples.ko: 아파트 골조에 문제가 있어서 점검을 받았어요.
examples.en: There was a problem with the apartment's frame, so it was inspected.

examples.ko: 철근으로 골조를 세운 뒤에 벽을 만들어요.
examples.en: After putting up the frame with steel bars, they build the walls.

explain: 건물이 서 있게 받쳐 주는 뼈대를 말해요. 공사 현장이나 건축 뉴스에서 많이 나오고, 일상에서는 '뼈대'라고도 해요. 벽이나 내부 장식은 골조가 끝난 뒤에 만들어요.
explain_en: It is the skeleton that holds up a building. It appears a lot at construction sites and in building news; in daily talk people also say '뼈대'. Walls and interior finishing come after the frame is done.

examples.en: This room has only one light source, so it's dark.

examples.ko: 사진을 찍을 때는 광원의 위치가 중요해요.
examples.en: When taking photos, the position of the light source matters.
The moon is not a light source that shines by itself.
The farther you get from the light source, the weaker the light becomes.

examples.ko: 광원을 책상 왼쪽에 두면 그림자가 덜 생겨요.
examples.en: If you put the light on the left of the desk, there are fewer shadows.

examples.ko: 이 전등은 광원이 눈에 직접 보이지 않게 만들었어요.
examples.en: This lamp is designed so the light source isn't directly visible.

explain: 일상에서는 '조명'이나 '불빛'이라고 하고, '광원'은 과학, 사진, 디자인처럼 빛이 나오는 근원을 따질 때 써요. 태양, 전구, 촛불처럼 스스로 빛을 내는 것을 가리켜요.
explain_en: In daily life people say '조명' or '불빛', while '광원' is used in science, photography and design when talking about where light comes from. It refers to things that give off light themselves, like the sun, a bulb or a candle.

examples.ko: 그물코가 너무 커서 작은 물고기는 빠져나가요.
examples.en: The mesh is so big that small fish slip through.

examples.ko: 어부가 찢어진 그물코를 한 땀씩 꿰맸어요.
examples.en: The fisherman mended the torn mesh stitch by stitch.
Sunlight shone through the holes of the net.
The tighter the mesh, the more fish you catch.
My finger got caught in the net and was hard to pull out.
This net has a really tight mesh.

explain: 그물에 뚫린 구멍 하나하나를 가리켜요. '촘촘하다', '성기다', '크다', '작다' 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to each hole in a net. It often appears with words like '촘촘하다' (tight), '성기다' (loose), '크다' (big) and '작다' (small).

examples.en: The chair's screw came loose, so it wobbles.
Please turn the screw with a screwdriver and tighten it.
I lost one small screw.
The screw in my glasses fell out, so I went to the optician.

examples.ko: 책상을 조립하려고 나사를 열 개 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought ten screws to assemble the desk.
This screw is too short.

explain: '나사를 조이다', '나사를 풀다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요. '못'은 망치로 박지만, '나사'는 돌려서 박는 것이라 구별돼요. 드라이버로 돌리는 도구는 '드라이버'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 요즘 팀 분위기에 나사가 풀린 것 같아요.
phrases.en: to get slack; to lose focus
phrases.nuance_ko: 나사가 풀린 기계처럼 사람이나 분위기가 느슨해지고 정신을 놓았다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like a machine whose screw has come loose, a person or mood has become slack and lost focus.

explain_en: The verbs are set: 나사를 조이다 (tighten) and 나사를 풀다 (loosen). 못 (nail) is hammered in, while 나사 is turned in. The tool you turn it with is a 드라이버 (screwdriver).

examples.en: Electronic parts are attached by soldering.
I burned my finger while soldering.

examples.ko: 이 회로는 납땜이 잘못돼서 작동하지 않아요.
examples.en: This circuit doesn't work because the soldering was done wrong.
It's my first time soldering, so it's a bit hard.

examples.ko: 고장 난 이어폰 선을 납땜해서 다시 썼어요.
examples.en: I soldered the broken earphone wire and used it again.
The soldering iron is hot, so be careful.

explain: '납땜하다'로도 쓰고, 함께 쓰는 도구는 '인두'예요. 땜납을 녹여서 금속을 붙이는 방법이에요. '용접'은 철판처럼 큰 금속을 붙일 때 많이 쓰는 말이라 작은 전자 부품에는 '납땜'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It also works as '납땜하다', and the tool used is a '인두' (soldering iron). It is a way of joining metal by melting solder. '용접' (welding) is more used for joining large metal such as steel plates, so for small electronic parts people say '납땜'.

examples.en: This door handle is made of brass.
Brass gets darker in color as it ages.
My grandmother's house has a brass candlestick.
When you polish brass, it shines brightly.

examples.ko: 놋쇠 종은 소리가 맑고 오래 울려요.
examples.en: A brass bell has a clear sound that rings for a long time.
Brass and copper look similar in color.

explain: 영어의 brass에 해당하고 '황동'이라고도 해요. 옛 물건이나 전통 물건 이야기에서 '놋쇠'가 잘 나오고, 일상에서는 '황동'이 더 설명하는 말처럼 들려요.
explain_en: It corresponds to English 'brass' and is also called '황동'. 놋쇠 shows up often when talking about old or traditional objects, while 황동 sounds more technical.

examples.en: Mom hung the garlic under the eaves.

examples.ko: 줄에 종을 달아매면 바람이 불 때 소리가 나요.
examples.en: If you hang a bell on the string, it rings when the wind blows.
I'm hanging radish greens on the wall to dry them.
Please hang the swing firmly on the tree.
I brought a chair to hang the balloons from the ceiling.
Who hung the sign up that high?

explain: 줄이나 끈으로 단단히 묶어서 걸어 놓는 느낌이 있어요. 일상에서는 '매달다'를 더 자주 말하고, '달아매다'는 '달아매요/달아맸어요'처럼 활용해요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of tying something firmly with a rope or string and leaving it hanging. In daily speech '매달다' is used more often, and 달아매다 conjugates as '달아매요/달아맸어요'.

examples.en: I bought a stand for the flower pot.
With a laptop stand, your neck feels better.
A statue stands on the pedestal.
I propped up the books with a support so they wouldn't fall.

examples.ko: 이 받침대는 높이를 바꿀 수 있어요.
examples.en: The height of this stand can be changed.
Please set your phone upright on the stand.

explain: 받침대는 물건 밑에서 받쳐 주는 도구를 넓게 말해요. 휴대폰이나 태블릿을 세워 두는 것은 보통 '거치대', 컵 밑에 까는 것은 '컵받침'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 받침대 broadly means anything that props up an object from below. A holder that keeps a phone or tablet upright is usually called 거치대, and a coaster under a cup is 컵받침.

examples.en: They are repairing the old bridge.

examples.ko: 낡은 지붕을 보수해야 비가 안 새요.
examples.en: You have to repair the old roof to stop the leaks.
The city repaired the road.

examples.ko: 한옥을 보수하는 일은 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Repairing a hanok takes a long time.
There isn't enough money to repair the building.

examples.ko: 보수한 곳이 다시 무너질까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried the repaired part will collapse again.

explain: 건물·다리·도로처럼 큰 시설의 낡거나 상한 곳을 고칠 때 써요. 작은 물건이나 기계에는 '고치다'나 '수리하다'를 써요. 소리가 같은 '보수'는 급여나 정치 성향을 뜻하기도 해서 문장 속에서 구분해야 해요.
explain_en: It is for fixing worn or damaged parts of large structures such as buildings, bridges and roads. For small items or machines use 고치다 or 수리하다. The sound 보수 also means pay or a conservative leaning, so tell them apart from context.

examples.ko: 용접할 때는 꼭 보안경을 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear safety glasses when welding.

examples.ko: 실험실에는 보안경 없이 들어가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't enter the lab without safety goggles.

examples.ko: 보안경이 김이 서려서 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: My goggles are fogged up, so I can't see well.

examples.ko: 공사 현장에서 보안경과 안전모를 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: At the construction site, they handed out goggles and hard hats.

examples.ko: 이 보안경은 안경 위에 겹쳐 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: These goggles can be worn over glasses.
I protected my eyes with safety glasses.

explain: 먼지, 파편, 약품 같은 것에서 눈을 지키려고 쓰는 안경이에요. 햇빛을 막는 선글라스와는 쓰임이 달라요. '보호안경'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: These are glasses worn to protect the eyes from dust, fragments and chemicals. They differ from sunglasses, which block sunlight. People also say '보호안경'.

examples.en: My father cut the rusty lock with a hacksaw.
A hacksaw has finer teeth than a wood saw.
I bought a new hacksaw blade at the hardware store.
My arm hurts after sawing with the hacksaw for a long time.
It's hard to cut a steel pipe with a hacksaw.

examples.ko: 쇠톱을 쓸 때는 장갑을 껴야 해요.
examples.en: You have to wear gloves when you use a hacksaw.

explain: 나무를 자르는 톱과 달리 쇠를 자를 때 쓰는 톱이에요. 철물점이나 공구 이야기에서 나와요. '쇠톱질'처럼 '질'을 붙이면 톱으로 자르는 동작을 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike a saw for cutting wood, this is the saw used for cutting metal, and it comes up when talking about hardware stores and tools. Adding '질' as in '쇠톱질' refers to the action of sawing with it.

examples.en: This coffee grinder is the manual type.
It's a manual door, so you have to push it by hand.

examples.ko: 전기가 나가도 수동식 펌프는 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even when the power goes out, you can use a manual pump.

examples.ko: 수동식과 자동식 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which is better, manual or automatic?
These days manual washing machines are hard to find.
If you switch to the manual type, it's much cheaper.

explain: 반대말은 '자동식'이에요. '수동'만 쓰면 '수동 모드'처럼 손으로 하는 방식을 말하고, 문법에서는 '수동태'처럼 '당하는 쪽'이라는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '자동식' (automatic type). '수동' alone, as in '수동 모드', means doing it by hand, and in grammar it also means 'passive', as in '수동태'.

examples.ko: 문이 닫히지 않게 문 밑에 쐐기를 끼웠어요.
examples.en: I put a wedge under the door so it wouldn't close.
The wedge came out, so the chair leg wobbles.

examples.ko: 쐐기 모양 조각이 틈에 딱 맞았어요.
examples.en: The wedge-shaped piece fit the gap perfectly.

examples.ko: 이 쐐기는 바람에 문이 닫히는 걸 막아 줘요.
examples.en: This wedge keeps the door from slamming shut in the wind.

examples.ko: 쐐기로 틈을 메우니 책상이 안 흔들려요.
examples.en: I filled the gap with a wedge, and the desk doesn't wobble anymore.

examples.ko: 쐐기처럼 뾰족한 돌이 바위틈에 박혀 있었어요.
examples.en: A wedge-like pointed stone was stuck in a rock crevice.

explain: 틈에 박아 고정하거나 벌릴 때 쓰는 한쪽이 뾰족한 물건이에요. 일상에서는 문받침이나 흔들리는 가구 밑에 끼우는 것을 떠올리면 돼요. '쐐기를 박다'는 일을 확실히 끝낼 때 쓰는 말로도 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 마지막 골로 우리 팀이 승부에 쐐기를 박았어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기나 협상에서 결과가 뒤집히지 않게 확실히 굳힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you make an outcome in a game or negotiation certain so it can't be reversed.
phrases.en_equiv: seal the deal; clinch the win

explain_en: It is an object with one pointed end, driven into a gap to fix things in place or pry them apart. In daily life, think of a doorstop or a piece under a wobbly piece of furniture. '쐐기를 박다' is also a common expression for settling something decisively.

examples.en: This desk is made of solid wood, so it is sturdy.

examples.ko: 원목 가구는 관리하기 까다롭지만 오래 써요.
examples.en: Solid wood furniture is fussy to care for, but it lasts a long time.

examples.ko: 숲에서 베어 낸 원목을 트럭으로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: They moved the logs cut from the forest by truck.
It's a solid wood floor, so it feels warm to walk barefoot.

examples.ko: 원목과 합판은 가격 차이가 많이 나요.
examples.en: There's a big price difference between solid wood and plywood.

examples.ko: 원목이라 너무 무거워서 혼자 못 옮겨요.
examples.en: It's solid wood, so it's too heavy for me to move alone.

explain: 가구나 바닥재 이야기에서는 합판이 아니라 진짜 나무를 그대로 쓴 것을 말해요. 가공하기 전의 통나무를 가리킬 때도 써요. 반대로 얇은 나무를 붙여 만든 것은 '합판'이라고 해요.
explain_en: When talking about furniture or flooring, it means real wood used as is, not plywood. It can also refer to raw logs before processing. The opposite, thin layers of wood glued together, is called '합판'.

examples.ko: 새해 아침에 정결한 마음으로 소원을 빌었어요.
examples.en: On New Year's morning, I made a wish with a pure heart.
My grandmother always keeps her room neat and clean.

examples.ko: 절에 들어가기 전에 손을 씻고 몸을 정결하게 했어요.
examples.en: Before entering the temple, I washed my hands and made myself clean.
The house was neat and clean, so the guests felt comfortable.

examples.ko: 정결하지 않은 손으로 음식을 만지지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't touch the food with unclean hands.
The yard of that temple is really clean and tidy.

explain: '깨끗하다'보다 단정하고 맑아서 마음이 경건해지는 느낌이 있어요. 몸, 마음, 공간에 쓰고, 일상 청소 이야기에는 '깨끗하다'를 쓰는 편이에요. 종교나 의식, 글에서 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Compared with '깨끗하다', it feels tidy and pure in a way that inspires reverence. It is used for the body, mind and spaces, while everyday cleaning talk uses '깨끗하다'. It fits religious settings, ceremonies and writing better.

examples.ko: 이 과자는 색소로 착색해서 색이 진해요.
examples.en: This snack is colored with dye, so the color is deep.

examples.ko: 식품을 착색할 때는 안전한 재료를 써야 해요.
examples.en: When coloring food, you must use safe ingredients.
At the factory, they tint the glass blue.
If you color it with natural ingredients, the color is subtle.

examples.ko: 이 사탕은 인공 색소로 착색하지 않았어요.
examples.en: This candy is not colored with artificial dye.

examples.ko: 나무를 갈색으로 착색했더니 훨씬 고급스러워 보여요.
examples.en: After I stained the wood brown, it looks much more high-class.

explain: 식품, 유리, 나무처럼 원래 색이 없거나 다른 것에 색을 입힐 때 쓰고, 식품 성분 표시나 제품 설명에서 자주 보여요. 일상에서 그림을 칠할 때는 '색칠하다', '물들이다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when adding color to things like food, glass or wood, and it often appears in ingredient labels and product descriptions. For painting a picture in daily life, use '색칠하다' or '물들이다'.

examples.en: You have to sew the stitches closely for the clothes to be sturdy.
Photos are packed closely together on the wall.

examples.ko: 이 일정표는 하루가 촘촘히 짜여 있어요.
examples.en: This schedule has every day packed tightly.

examples.ko: 모종을 촘촘히 심으면 잘 자라지 않아요.
examples.en: If you plant seedlings too close together, they don't grow well.
Stars are studded thickly across the night sky.

examples.ko: 그물을 촘촘히 짜서 작은 물고기도 잡혀요.
examples.en: The net is woven tightly, so even small fish get caught.

explain: 형용사 '촘촘하다'의 부사형이에요. 간격이 좁을 때뿐 아니라 일정이나 계획이 빈틈없이 짜여 있을 때도 써요. 반대로 간격이 넓고 드문 모양은 '듬성듬성'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It's the adverb form of the adjective '촘촘하다'. It's used not only for narrow gaps but also for schedules or plans that are packed with no free time. The opposite, with wide and sparse gaps, is '듬성듬성'.

examples.en: I looked for pliers to cut the wire.
I pulled out the nail with pliers.
There should be a pair of pliers in the toolbox.
My father fixed the bike chain with pliers.

examples.ko: 펜치 좀 빌려 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you lend me your pliers?

examples.ko: 이 펜치는 손잡이가 미끄럽지 않아서 좋아요.
examples.en: These pliers are good because the handles aren't slippery.

explain: 물건을 잡거나 철사를 자르고 구부릴 때 쓰는 공구예요. 손잡이를 쥐어 물건을 꽉 집어요. 끝이 뾰족한 것은 '롱노즈'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a tool for gripping, cutting and bending wire. You squeeze the handles to hold things tightly. The pointed-tip type is often called '롱노즈'.
